diagnosis.root_cause: Duplicate RADIUS radcheck rows exist for the same username, with conflicting line IDs. FreeRADIUS is resolving the rows inconsistently, causing repeated authentication/session disconnects.
evidence: The subscriber has 19 sessions in 24 hours, exceeding the 8-session flapping threshold, and the average session duration is only 38 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean.
The optical link is healthy: RX is -20.62 dBm in the normal band, TX is 2.44 dBm in the normal band, and the seven-day RX/TX variation is within the healthy noise floor.
TX bias current is stable around 10.6 mA, so there is no evidence of laser degradation.
Distance remains constant at 96, so there is no path or record distance change.
All tested peers on EPON0/5 are online with normal optical readings, ruling out an ONU, splitter, PON-port, or shared infrastructure fault.
The OLT, router, VLAN, and live ONU probes are healthy and responding, with the customer currently online and using the expected VLAN 1055.
RADIUS contains two radcheck rows for the same username, one matching the active CRM line ID and one orphan row with a conflicting line ID; resolution depends on which row FreeRADIUS reaches first.
Because the physical layer is clean and the authentication records conflict on the same server, the presenting fault is authentication session flapping rather than signal flapping or replication lag.

remediation.action: Remove the orphan radcheck row carrying lineid 1C:EF:03:90:2B:5A, retain and reconcile the row for lineid 00:A1:07:C4:1D:88, then terminate stale sessions and verify that subsequent authentication consistently assigns the correct line ID and IP.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two radcheck rows exist for the same username. FreeRADIUS resolves inconsistently between them, so authentication succeeds or fails depending on which row is matched, producing repeated short sessions and two alternating IP assignments.
expected_reasoning: 19 sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline, with a 38 minute mean duration against an 11.9 hour norm
RX has been flat at -20.6 dBm for seven days inside the +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so signal is not the cause
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable
Port neighbours are normal and the OLT is healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault
With no optical explanation available, the search moves to the authentication layer
RADIUS holds two radcheck rows for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, one of them an orphan with a different lineid
Recent sessions alternate between two IP addresses, consistent with inconsistent row resolution
Traffic is erratic rather than declining, which fits intermittent authentication rather than a degrading link

expected_escalation.review_reason: Duplicate RADIUS rows must be resolved by hand; deleting the wrong row disconnects the customer

distractors: The session pattern is identical to signal-related flapping and invites that diagnosis
Zero-throughput windows in the speed series look like link loss but coincide with rejected auth
ONU is a Router type, inviting a CPE-fault explanation
